title: Noise-Cancelling Headphones Fight Sound With Sound
fb_caption: Noise-cancelling headphones don't just block outside sound. Tiny microphones on the ear cups listen to the noise around you, and a chip makes a matching sound wave, flipped upside down. When the two waves meet, the peaks fill the dips and much of the hum cancels out. It works best on steady, low hums like an air conditioner or an engine; voices are higher and keep changing, so more of them gets through. Where do you wear yours the most?
engagement_comment: Where do you wear yours the most? 1 = on a plane, 2 = on my commute, 3 = at my desk.

beats.text: Noise-cancelling headphones don't just block outside sound. They actually fight sound with more sound.
Tiny microphones on the ear cups listen to the noise around you, like the hum of an air conditioner.
A chip inside makes a matching sound wave, flipped upside down, and plays it through the speakers.
When the two waves meet, the peaks fill the dips, so much of that hum cancels out.
Here's the twist. It works best on steady, low hums. Voices are higher and keep changing, so more gets through.
Where do you wear yours the most: on a plane, on your commute, or at your desk? Tell us below.
